quiz.question: Which of these techniques is fundamentally about splitting data across multiple servers so each one handles a fraction of the total?
options: Caching frequently accessed data in memory
Adding indexes to speed up queries
quiz.explanation: Sharding partitions data (here, view counters by video ID) so each server owns only part of the load.

quiz.question: Which data structure efficiently maintains the K largest counts as views stream in?
quiz.explanation: Compare each new count with the heap's smallest element; only larger ones replace it, in O(log K).

quiz.question: What is the main trade-off of approximate counting such as a Count-Min Sketch?
options: It can overestimate counts, giving up precision
quiz.explanation: Sketches use tiny, fixed memory but can over-count — a problem when the requirement is precise top-K.

quiz.question: How can top-K for a sliding window (e.g. the last hour) be maintained?
options: Add new views and subtract views as they leave the window
quiz.explanation: Processing both the head and the tail of the stream keeps window counts current without full recomputation.
